Unit tests for LateFeeCalculator

Task

Write pytest-style unit tests for the court-finance LateFeeCalculator class. The tests must reach more than 90% branch coverage.

Approach

  • Every test passes a fixed today, so results do not depend on the real date.
  • Dates are anchored on Monday 2026-09-07. Weekday counts were worked out by hand.
  • Expected fees are worked out from the rules, not copied from the code's output.

Branch map

BranchTest that covers it
today or date.today() (both sides)test_defaults_today_to_date_today, all others
end <= start true / falsetest_weekday_days_between (parametrized)
while loop, weekday true / falsetest_weekday_days_between (weekend cases)
balance_cents <= 0 true / falsetest_non_positive_balance_has_no_fee, fee tests
billable_days <= 0 true / falsegrace tests and fee tests
min() picks cap / roundedtest_fee_capped_at_25_percent, test_fee_scales_by_billable_days
max() picks minimum / cappedtest_minimum_fee_applies, test_minimum_overrides_cap

Answer: test_late_fee_calculator.py

import pytest
from datetime import date

from late_fee_calculator import LateFeeCalculator  # adjust to your module path

# Monday 2026-09-07 is the anchor due date for most tests.
DUE = date(2026, 9, 7)  # Monday


def calc(today):
    return LateFeeCalculator(today=today)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Construction
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_defaults_today_to_date_today():
    assert LateFeeCalculator()._today == date.today()


def test_explicit_today_is_used():
    assert LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2030, 1, 2))._today == date(2030, 1, 2)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# _weekday_days_between
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "start, end, expected",
    [
        (date(2026, 9, 7), date(2026, 9, 7), 0),    # same day
        (date(2026, 9, 8), date(2026, 9, 7), 0),    # end before start
        (date(2026, 9, 7), date(2026, 9, 8), 1),    # Mon -> Tue
        (date(2026, 9, 7), date(2026, 9, 14), 5),   # Mon -> next Mon
        (date(2026, 9, 7), date(2026, 9, 12), 5),   # Mon -> Sat (end exclusive)
        (date(2026, 9, 11), date(2026, 9, 14), 1),  # Fri -> Mon (only Fri counts)
        (date(2026, 9, 12), date(2026, 9, 14), 0),  # Sat -> Mon (weekend only)
        (date(2026, 9, 7), date(2026, 9, 21), 10),  # two full weeks
    ],
)
def test_weekday_days_between(start, end, expected):
    assert calc(date(2026, 1, 1))._weekday_days_between(start, end) == expected


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# No fee cases
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize("balance", [0, -1, -1_000_000])
def test_non_positive_balance_has_no_fee(balance):
    # Very late, but balance is not positive, so the fee is 0.
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 21)).compute_fee_cents(balance, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 0


def test_not_yet_due_has_no_fee():
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 1)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 0


def test_due_today_has_no_fee():
    assert calc(DUE).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 0


def test_within_grace_period_has_no_fee():
    # 2026-09-21 is exactly 10 weekdays after 2026-09-07, so billable_days == 0.
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 21)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 0


def test_weekends_extend_effective_grace():
    # 14 calendar days late but only 10 weekdays, so still no fee.
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 21)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 0


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fee calculation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_first_billable_day():
    # Tue 2026-09-22 -> 11 weekdays -> 1 billable day.
    # 2,000,000 * (0.015/30) * 1 = 1000
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 22)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 1000


def test_fee_scales_by_billable_days():
    # Fri 2026-09-25 -> 14 weekdays -> 4 billable days -> 4000
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 25)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 4000


def test_weekend_days_do_not_add_fee():
    # Sat 09-26 and Mon 09-28 both count 15 weekdays (5 billable) since Sat/Sun are skipped.
    sat = calc(date(2026, 9, 26)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE)
    mon = calc(date(2026, 9, 28)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE)
    assert sat == mon == 5000


def test_due_date_on_weekend():
    # Due Sat 2026-09-05; Tue 2026-09-22 -> 11 weekdays -> 1 billable day.
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 22)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, date(2026, 9, 5)) == 1000


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "balance, expected",
    [
        (2_000_600, 1000),  # raw 1000.3 -> rounds down
        (2_000_800, 1000),  # raw 1000.4 -> rounds down
        (2_001_200, 1001),  # raw 1000.6 -> rounds up
        (2_001_800, 1001),  # raw 1000.9 -> rounds up
    ],
)
def test_rounds_to_whole_cents(balance, expected):
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 22)).compute_fee_cents(balance, DUE) == expected


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimum and maximum
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_minimum_fee_applies():
    # 10,000 * 0.0005 * 1 = 5 cents, raised to the $5 (500 cent) minimum.
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 22)).compute_fee_cents(10_000, DUE) == 500


def test_fee_capped_at_25_percent():
    # Due Mon 2024-01-01, today Mon 2026-09-21 -> 710 weekdays -> 700 billable.
    # raw = 10,000 * 0.0005 * 700 = 3500, cap = 2500.
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 21)).compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 2500


def test_fee_just_under_cap_is_not_capped():
    # 14 weekdays -> 4 billable; 2,000,000 -> 4000, well under the 500,000 cap.
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 25)).compute_fee_cents(2_000_000, DUE) == 4000


def test_minimum_overrides_cap_for_small_balances():
    # balance 1000: cap = 250 cents, raw = 350 -> capped to 250 -> raised to the 500 minimum.
    assert calc(date(2026, 9, 21)).compute_fee_cents(1_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 500

Notes

  • Run with pytest --cov=late_fee_calculator --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing. I expect 100% of branches to be covered. I worked this out by hand and did not run the suite.
  • The rounding tests use fractional parts of .3, .4, .6 and .9 on purpose. An exact .5 depends on floating-point error in 0.015/30, so it would make the tests flaky.
  • test_minimum_overrides_cap_for_small_balances records a spec ambiguity. The minimum fee of $5 can exceed the 25% cap, and the code lets the minimum win. If the cap should win, that test should change with the code.
  • test_defaults_today_to_date_today could fail if the test runs across midnight. Patch date if that matters to you.
